content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: high token delta detected for customer CascadeBio (vpc-dedicated pool). Paging on-call.
ava: got the page, pulling up cluster and metering. any customers impacted beyond billing noise?
rohit: I'm on infra. Preliminary: a spike in token_count ingestion for CascadeBio tenant id cb-88 on the dedicated-pool-5 between 03:12-03:20 UTC. No error surge in requests, just higher token totals.
claire: tagging SRE & Billing. @billing-bot can you snapshot the last 24h meter export for cb-88 and compare to tokens_seen by runtime?
billing-bot: snapshot job queued (job id: sb-4492). Export URL: https://internal.s3/redwood/exports/sb-4492.csv (expires in 1h)
ben: I'm in the runtime logs. Seeing a lot of repeated system prompts from their agent side — long context windows. Example log tail:
```
2026-03-14T03:14:02Z cb-88 request_id=0a3f model=gpt-compat seq_len=4096 tokens=3872 prompt_snippet="[REDACTED LONG PROMPT FROM CASCADE]
2026-03-14T03:14:04Z cb-88 request_id=0a40 model=gpt-compat seq_len=4096 tokens=4090 prompt_snippet="[REDACTED LONG PROMPT FROM CASCADE]"
```
rohit: runtime shows normal QPS. This looks like a client-side change that began rolling at ~03:12. Could be a malformed SDK call sending huge context repeatedly.
maria: contacting the account rep now to ask if they rolled any prompt changes. cc @claire
ava: ok let's confirm whether metering counted these as billable tokens or if a duplicate ingestion/ETL bug inflated the meter. @billing-bot please run a quick reconciliation: meter_table.tokens_ingested vs runtime.token_events deduped by request_id.
billing-bot: reconciler started. Preliminary diff: meter_table shows 1,248,560 tokens; runtime deduped events show 312,140 tokens for 03:00-04:00 UTC. (+936,420 tokens unexplained)
claire: that's big. Could be double-counted rows on the metering collector or a misrouted batching job aggregating across tenants. Rohit, any recent deploys to metering pipeline last 24h?
rohit: metering pipeline v2.3 deployed yesterday at 22:00 UTC. No hotfixes since. I'm checking connector logs now.
ben: I captured the collector worker logs — looks like worker-12 retried a batch and the dedupe_key was null for some records. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T02:59:58Z collector worker-12 INFO batch=8245 tenant=cb-88 dedupe_key=null
2026-03-14T03:00:10Z collector worker-12 ERROR retrying batch 8245 cause=timeout
2026-03-14T03:00:11Z collector worker-12 INFO batch=8245 tenant=cb-88 published rows=5
```
maria: the account rep responded: they did a config change to always include the full transcript in the system prompt (large), rolled at 03:11. So client change + collector retry==likely double count.
ava: mitigation plan: 1) pause billing ingestion for cb-88 window 03:00-04:00; 2) mark suspect rows and run dedupe by request_id and timestamp; 3) reach out to customer to roll back immediate change if they want. Who can pause the ingestion?
rohit: I can flip the metering ingestion switch for cb-88 to 'paused' in 2mins. Will also snapshot the raw event stream.
claire: Ben, can you prepare a short runbook we can show CSM and the customer: what we will do to adjust their invoice and timeline?
ben: on it. Draft runbook: - Pause ingestion for cb-88 03:00-04:00 UTC. - Run dedupe using runtime request_id. - If dedupe removes >90% of extra tokens, adjust billed tokens to runtime deduped count and issue credit. - If not, escalate for deeper forensic.
maria: CSM confirmed: customer will revert the prompt change if we can guarantee credits for accidental spike. They're sensitive because this is a private VPC contract.
ava: executing pause now. @rohit once paused, post the command you ran.
rohit: ran: ```
POST /internal/metering/tenants/cb-88/pause
{ "until": "2026-03-14T05:00:00Z", "reason": "incident 1932506789 pause for dedupe" }
```
rohit: ingestion paused. snapshot id: snap-7732
billing-bot: reconciler completed. Suggested action: mark rows with dedupe_key null and request_id duplicates as suspect (count: 921,230 tokens). See /internal/reports/sb-4492-recon.json
claire: we have enough evidence to treat this as non-billable. Maria, confirm with legal/finance if we can issue immediate provisional credit and follow with final reconciliation.
maria: looping in finance now. @billing-bot please create provisional credit memo for cb-88 amount=estimated tokens 921230 * $0.0006 = $552.74, tag=INC-1932506789
billing-bot: provisional credit created: CM-9901 (pending finance approval)
ben: customer-facing message draft:
"We saw an automated increase in tokens billed between 03:00-04:00 UTC due to a recent client-side prompt change combined with collector retries. We've paused ingestion for that window and are issuing a provisional credit while we complete a final reconciliation. No further action required on your side unless you want to revert the prompt change."
maria: customer replies: please do revert now. They've pushed a rollback at 03:40 and confirm normal prompt lengths resumed.
ava: good. timeline summary: client change 03:11 -> collector retry + dedupe_key null -> double-counting persisted until pause at 03:24. Customer rollback at 03:40. We'll finalize recon by EOD.
claire: postmortem action items: 1) add strict dedupe_key enforcement in collector, reject rows without dedupe_key. 2) add alert when meter_table vs runtime token delta > 10% for any tenant. 3) add UI control for provisional credits.
rohit: agreed. I'll open infra tickets and link.
ben: closing notes: assigning follow-ups: INF-662 (collector dedupe fix) assigned to rohit, BILL-447 (reconciliation automation) assigned to billing team, CS-331 (customer communication) assigned to maria.
ops-bot: Incident INC-1932506789 transitioned to "monitoring". :white_check_mark:
claire: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread for updates.
